SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.68
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the typical strong benzene-ring breathing at 1004 cm⁻¹ and an intense ring C=C stretch at 1618 cm⁻¹, indicating a single substituted aromatic ring.  The carbonyl stretch of a hydrogen-bonded aromatic carboxylic acid is known to shift down to ~1620 cm⁻¹; the 1618 cm⁻¹ band matches this behaviour, consistent with the intramolecularly H-bonded COOH found only in salicylic acid (candidate 1).  Supporting bands that match reported Raman data for salicylic acid include 763 cm⁻¹ (out-of-plane ring deformation), 1298/1319 cm⁻¹ (C–O and C–OH bends), 1232 cm⁻¹ (in-plane O–H bend), 1167 cm⁻¹ and 1079 cm⁻¹ (C–H in-plane bends), and 3081 cm⁻¹ (aromatic C–H stretch).  Halogenated acids (candidates 2–3) or aldehydes/amides (4–9) lack this low-frequency carbonyl band, and multi-ring compound 8 would give additional phenyl peaks not observed.  Therefore the spectrum best fits O=C(O)c1cccc(O)c1.
